So far everything has been made of separate pieces. First atoms: even the
[blast wave](../webgpu-blast-wave/) was a wave of atoms shoving one another. Then
[darts](../webgpu-darts-in-many-dimensions/), [walkers](../webgpu-metropolis-walkers/) and
the [needles of a magnet](../webgpu-ising-model/), all pushed about by chance. This post
has no atoms and no dice.

Drop a pebble in a pond and a ring spreads out. Nothing travels with the ring: the water
only moves up and down, a little, and the shape of that moving goes on across the pond.
A wave is that shape. It is a thing in its own right, and it does things that no single
particle does. It bends round corners, it passes through other waves, and where two meet
it can cancel.

The tank below is a sheet of water seen from above. Red is a crest, blue is a trough and
dark is flat. **Click anywhere to drop a pebble**, or drag to drop a line of them.

Try these:

- _Drop one pebble._ The ring grows and fades. It fades because the same wave has to
  cover a longer and longer circle, so each stretch of it gets weaker.
- _Switch Source to Plane wave and Barrier to Gap._ A wall with a hole in it. When the
  hole is much wider than the wavelength, a beam goes through. Make the **Wavelength**
  longer and the hole is small by comparison: the beam gives way to a ring, as if
  the hole were a pebble.
- _Choose Double slit._ Two holes make two rings, and where they overlap the waves add.
  Crest on crest is a bigger crest, and crest on trough is flat water. The calm lines
  fanning out are the interference pattern.
- _Push the Courant number just over 0.7._ This one is about the computer, not the water. It
  is explained [below](#why-the-timestep-has-a-limit).

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| column: screen-inset
//| code-fold: true
//| code-summary: "Show code"
{
  // Shared WebGPU boilerplate: setup, buffers and the animation loop (lib/gpu.js)
  const gpu = await import(new URL("../lib/gpu.js", document.baseURI).href);
  const ui = await import(new URL("../lib/ui.js", document.baseURI).href);

  // Controls are read live from their elements, so moving them does not restart
  // this cell.
  const sourceInput = viewof tankSource;
  const barrierInput = viewof tankBarrier;
  const wavelengthInput = viewof wavelength;
  const speedInput = viewof waveSpeed; // log10 of cells a second
  const courantInput = viewof courant;

  const { canvas, device, context, format } = await gpu.setup({
    width: 640,
    height: 360,
    resolution: "auto",
  });
  canvas.style.touchAction = "none";

  // The tank, in cells, and where things sit in it
  const W = 640;
  const H = 360;
  const cells = W * H;
  const groupSide = 16;
  const beachWidth = 24; // cells of damping at each edge
  const sourceX = 28; // the paddle for the plane wave, just inside the beach
  const wallX = 196; // left side of a barrier
  const wallWidth = 8;
  const screenX = 592; // the far wall, where the pattern is measured
  const slitWidth = 16;
  const slitSpacing = 64;
  const gapWidth = 32;
  const amplitude = 0.25; // height of the plane wave
  const maxSplashes = 8;

  // Whether each cell is water (1) or a wall (0)
  function buildDepth(kind) {
    const depth = new Float32Array(cells).fill(1);
    const wall = (x0, x1, y0, y1) => {
      for (let y = y0; y < y1; y++) for (let x = x0; x < x1; x++) depth[y * W + x] = 0;
    };
    const mid = H / 2;
    if (kind === "gap") {
      wall(wallX, wallX + wallWidth, 0, mid - gapWidth / 2);
      wall(wallX, wallX + wallWidth, mid + gapWidth / 2, H);
    } else if (kind === "double") {
      const top = mid - slitSpacing / 2;
      const bottom = mid + slitSpacing / 2;
      const half = slitWidth / 2;
      wall(wallX, wallX + wallWidth, 0, top - half);
      wall(wallX, wallX + wallWidth, top + half, bottom - half);
      wall(wallX, wallX + wallWidth, bottom + half, H);
    }
    return depth;
  }

  // --------------------------------------------------------------- the shaders
  const common = `
    struct Params {
      width: u32,
      height: u32,
      courant2: f32,
      sponge: f32,        // damping per step at the very edge of the tank
      edge: f32,          // width of the beach, in cells
      pad2: u32,
      sourceOn: u32,
      sourceX: u32,
      sourceAmp: f32,     // forcing added each step
      sourceOmega: f32,   // radians a step
      sourceStart: u32,   // step at which the source switched on
      rampSteps: f32,
      splashCount: u32,
      gain: f32,
      pad0: u32,
      pad1: u32,
      splashes: array<vec4f, ${maxSplashes}>, // x, y, height, radius
    }

    @group(0) @binding(0) var<uniform> params: Params;
    @group(0) @binding(1) var<storage, read> depth: array<f32>;

    // 0 in open water, rising to 1 at the border: how far into the beach a cell is
    fn beachFraction(x: u32, y: u32) -> f32 {
      let ex = min(f32(x), f32(params.width - 1u - x));
      let ey = min(f32(y), f32(params.height - 1u - y));
      let e = min(ex, ey);
      return select(0.0, (params.edge - e) / params.edge, e < params.edge);
    }
  `;

  const stepModule = device.createShaderModule({
    code: `
      ${common}
      @group(0) @binding(2) var<storage, read> before: array<f32>;
      @group(0) @binding(3) var<storage, read> now: array<f32>;
      @group(0) @binding(4) var<storage, read_write> after: array<f32>;
      @group(0) @binding(5) var<storage, read_write> clock: array<u32>;

      @compute @workgroup_size(${groupSide}, ${groupSide})
      fn step(@builtin(global_invocation_id) id: vec3u) {
        let w = params.width;
        let h = params.height;
        if (id.x >= w || id.y >= h) { return; }
        let x = id.x;
        let y = id.y;
        let i = y * w + x;
        let k = depth[i];
        let here = now[i];

        // Pull towards each neighbour, weighted by the smaller of the two cells'
        // depth: a wall (0) has nothing to pull on
        var pull = 0.0;
        if (x > 0u)     { pull += min(k, depth[i - 1u]) * (now[i - 1u] - here); }
        if (x + 1u < w) { pull += min(k, depth[i + 1u]) * (now[i + 1u] - here); }
        if (y > 0u)     { pull += min(k, depth[i - w]) * (now[i - w] - here); }
        if (y + 1u < h) { pull += min(k, depth[i + w]) * (now[i + w] - here); }

        let q = beachFraction(x, y);
        let sigma = params.sponge * q * q;
        var next = (2.0 * here - (1.0 - sigma) * before[i] + params.courant2 * pull) / (1.0 + sigma);

        // The plane-wave paddle adds to the water rather than fixing it, so waves
        // coming back from the barrier pass through it
        if (params.sourceOn == 1u && x == params.sourceX) {
          let t = f32(clock[0]) - f32(params.sourceStart);
          let ramp = smoothstep(0.0, 1.0, t / params.rampSteps);
          next += params.sourceAmp * ramp * cos(params.sourceOmega * t);
        }
        // Past the stability limit the numbers grow without bound: stop them
        // overflowing so the picture stays drawable
        after[i] = select(0.0, clamp(next, -1e6, 1e6), k > 0.0);
      }

      @compute @workgroup_size(1)
      fn tick() {
        clock[0] = clock[0] + 1u;
      }
    `,
  });
  const stepPipeline = device.createComputePipeline({
    layout: "auto",
    compute: { module: stepModule, entryPoint: "step" },
  });
  const tickPipeline = device.createComputePipeline({
    layout: "auto",
    compute: { module: stepModule, entryPoint: "tick" },
  });

  const splashModule = device.createShaderModule({
    code: `
      ${common}
      @group(0) @binding(2) var<storage, read_write> before: array<f32>;
      @group(0) @binding(3) var<storage, read_write> now: array<f32>;

      // A pebble: a dent with a ring round it, added to the surface and not moving to begin
      // with. The ring makes the dent add up to no net water, as a real splash does
      @compute @workgroup_size(${groupSide}, ${groupSide})
      fn splash(@builtin(global_invocation_id) id: vec3u) {
        if (id.x >= params.width || id.y >= params.height) { return; }
        let i = id.y * params.width + id.x;
        if (depth[i] == 0.0) { return; }
        var bump = 0.0;
        for (var n = 0u; n < params.splashCount; n++) {
          let s = params.splashes[n];
          let dx = f32(id.x) - s.x;
          let dy = f32(id.y) - s.y;
          let r2 = (dx * dx + dy * dy) / (2.0 * s.w * s.w);
          bump += s.z * (1.0 - r2) * exp(-r2);
        }
        now[i] += bump;
        before[i] += bump;
      }
    `,
  });
  const splashPipeline = device.createComputePipeline({
    layout: "auto",
    compute: { module: splashModule, entryPoint: "splash" },
  });

  const showModule = device.createShaderModule({
    code: `
      ${common}
      @group(0) @binding(3) var<storage, read> now: array<f32>;

      struct Out {
        @builtin(position) position: vec4f,
        @location(0) uv: vec2f,
      }

      @vertex
      fn showVertex(@location(0) corner: vec2f) -> Out {
        return Out(
          vec4f(corner, 0.0, 1.0),
          vec2f(corner.x * 0.5 + 0.5, 0.5 - corner.y * 0.5),
        );
      }

      @fragment
      fn showFragment(in: Out) -> @location(0) vec4f {
        let w = params.width;
        let h = params.height;
        let x = min(u32(in.uv.x * f32(w)), w - 1u);
        let y = min(u32(in.uv.y * f32(h)), h - 1u);
        let i = y * w + x;
        let k = depth[i];
        if (k == 0.0) { return vec4f(0.62, 0.62, 0.64, 1.0); }

        let flat = vec3f(0.10, 0.10, 0.10);
        let v = now[i] * params.gain;
        let crest = vec3f(1.0, 0.282, 0.204);   // #FF4834
        let trough = vec3f(0.22, 0.60, 0.85);
        var colour = mix(flat, select(trough, crest, v > 0.0), clamp(abs(v), 0.0, 1.0));
        colour *= 1.0 - 0.45 * beachFraction(x, y);
        if (params.sourceOn == 1u && (x == params.sourceX || x == params.sourceX + 1u)) {
          colour = vec3f(0.92);
        }
        return vec4f(colour, 1.0);
      }
    `,
  });
  const showPipeline = device.createRenderPipeline({
    layout: "auto",
    vertex: { module: showModule, entryPoint: "showVertex", buffers: [gpu.squareLayout] },
    fragment: { module: showModule, entryPoint: "showFragment", targets: [{ format }] },
    primitive: { topology: "triangle-list" },
  });

  // --------------------------------------------------------------------- buffers
  // Three height arrays that take turns: one step ago, now, and the one being made
  const heights = [0, 1, 2].map(() => gpu.storageBuffer(device, new Float32Array(cells)));
  const depthBuffer = gpu.storageBuffer(device, buildDepth("open"));
  const clock = gpu.storageBuffer(device, new Uint32Array(1));
  const snapshot = gpu.storageBuffer(device, new Float32Array(cells));
  const paramBuffer = device.createBuffer({
    size: 16 * 4 + maxSplashes * 16,
    usage: GPUBufferUsage.UNIFORM | GPUBufferUsage.COPY_DST,
  });
  const paramBytes = new ArrayBuffer(16 * 4 + maxSplashes * 16);
  const paramU32 = new Uint32Array(paramBytes);
  const paramF32 = new Float32Array(paramBytes);

  // Bind groups for each way the three arrays can be taking turns
  const stepGroups = [0, 1, 2].map((r) =>
    device.createBindGroup({
      layout: stepPipeline.getBindGroupLayout(0),
      entries: [
        { binding: 0, resource: { buffer: paramBuffer } },
        { binding: 1, resource: { buffer: depthBuffer } },
        { binding: 2, resource: { buffer: heights[r] } },
        { binding: 3, resource: { buffer: heights[(r + 1) % 3] } },
        { binding: 4, resource: { buffer: heights[(r + 2) % 3] } },
        { binding: 5, resource: { buffer: clock } },
      ],
    }),
  );
  const tickGroup = device.createBindGroup({
    layout: tickPipeline.getBindGroupLayout(0),
    entries: [{ binding: 5, resource: { buffer: clock } }],
  });
  const splashGroups = [0, 1, 2].map((r) =>
    device.createBindGroup({
      layout: splashPipeline.getBindGroupLayout(0),
      entries: [
        { binding: 0, resource: { buffer: paramBuffer } },
        { binding: 1, resource: { buffer: depthBuffer } },
        { binding: 2, resource: { buffer: heights[r] } },
        { binding: 3, resource: { buffer: heights[(r + 1) % 3] } },
      ],
    }),
  );
  const showGroups = [0, 1, 2].map((r) =>
    device.createBindGroup({
      layout: showPipeline.getBindGroupLayout(0),
      entries: [
        { binding: 0, resource: { buffer: paramBuffer } },
        { binding: 1, resource: { buffer: depthBuffer } },
        { binding: 3, resource: { buffer: heights[(r + 1) % 3] } },
      ],
    }),
  );
  const cornerBuffer = gpu.unitSquare(device);

  // ------------------------------------------------------------------- the state
  let turn = 0; // which of the three arrays is "one step ago"
  let stepCount = 0;
  let sourceStart = 0;
  const pebbles = []; // [x, y, height, radius] waiting to be dropped

  const drop = (x, y, height = 2) => {
    pebbles.push([x, y, height, 6]);
    if (pebbles.length > maxSplashes) pebbles.shift();
  };

  // Pebbles and drags
  let lastDrag = null;
  const place = (event) => {
    const box = canvas.getBoundingClientRect();
    return [((event.clientX - box.left) / box.width) * W, ((event.clientY - box.top) / box.height) * H];
  };
  canvas.addEventListener("pointerdown", (event) => {
    canvas.setPointerCapture(event.pointerId);
    lastDrag = place(event);
    drop(...lastDrag);
  });
  canvas.addEventListener("pointermove", (event) => {
    if (!lastDrag) return;
    const here = place(event);
    if (Math.hypot(here[0] - lastDrag[0], here[1] - lastDrag[1]) > 10) {
      lastDrag = here;
      drop(...here, 1.4);
    }
  });
  const release = () => (lastDrag = null);
  canvas.addEventListener("pointerup", release);
  canvas.addEventListener("pointercancel", release);

  // What the charts are built from
  const readback = gpu.readback(device, [{ buffer: snapshot, bytes: cells * 4 }]);
  const sampleEvery = 10; // frames between readbacks
  const keep = 400; // peak samples kept for the chart
  let frameCount = 0;
  let epoch = 0; // bumped when the tank is cleared, so a read in flight is dropped
  let statsStart = 0; // step at which the averaged pattern last restarted
  let peak = 0;
  const peakHistory = [];
  const brightness = new Float64Array(H); // summed squared height along the far wall
  let averaged = 0;

  const [screenHost, peakHost] = charts.children;
  const draw = ui.plotter(Plot);

  // The classic prediction for the pattern on a distant wall, for waves of this
  // wavelength through slits of width a that are d apart (d = 0 for one slit)
  function prediction(lambda) {
    const barrier = barrierInput.value;
    if (barrier !== "gap" && barrier !== "double") return null;
    const a = barrier === "gap" ? gapWidth : slitWidth;
    const d = barrier === "gap" ? 0 : slitSpacing;
    const distance = screenX - (wallX + wallWidth / 2);
    const rows = [];
    for (let y = -H / 2 + 20; y <= H / 2 - 20; y += 2) {
      const s = y / Math.hypot(y, distance);
      const alpha = (Math.PI * a * s) / lambda;
      const beta = (Math.PI * d * s) / lambda;
      const envelope = alpha === 0 ? 1 : (Math.sin(alpha) / alpha) ** 2;
      rows.push({ y, I: envelope * (d === 0 ? 1 : Math.cos(beta) ** 2) });
    }
    return rows;
  }

  function drawCharts() {
    const measured = [];
    if (averaged > 0) {
      let top = 0;
      for (let y = 20; y < H - 20; y++) top = Math.max(top, brightness[y]);
      for (let y = 20; y < H - 20; y++) measured.push({ y: y - H / 2, I: brightness[y] / top });
    }
    const theory = sourceInput.value === "plane" ? prediction(wavelengthInput.value) : null;
    draw(screenHost, {
      x: { label: "position along the far wall (cells from the middle)", grid: true },
      y: { label: "wave brightness (relative)", grid: true, domain: [0, 1.05] },
      marks: [
        Plot.line(measured, { x: "y", y: "I", stroke: "#FF4834" }),
        theory
          ? Plot.line(theory, {
              x: "y",
              y: "I",
              stroke: "currentColor",
              strokeOpacity: 0.7,
              strokeDasharray: "4 3",
            })
          : null,
      ],
    });
    draw(peakHost, {
      x: { label: "time steps", grid: true },
      y: { label: "largest wave height", grid: true, type: "log", domain: [1e-4, 1e6] },
      marks: [
        Plot.ruleY([1], { stroke: "currentColor", strokeOpacity: 0.2 }),
        Plot.line(peakHistory, { x: "t", y: "peak", stroke: "#FF4834", clip: true }),
      ],
    });
  }

  // Wait for the start-up transient to leave the far wall before averaging
  function settled() {
    const lambda = wavelengthInput.value;
    const C = courantInput.value;
    const travel = (screenX - sourceX) / C + (6 * lambda) / C;
    return stepCount - statsStart > travel;
  }

  function onData(buffer) {
    const u = new Float32Array(buffer);
    let top = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < cells; i++) top = Math.max(top, Math.abs(u[i]));
    peak = top;
    peakHistory.push({ t: stepCount, peak: Math.max(top, 1e-4) });
    if (peakHistory.length > keep) peakHistory.shift();
    if (sourceInput.value === "plane" && settled()) {
      for (let y = 0; y < H; y++) brightness[y] += u[y * W + screenX] ** 2;
      averaged++;
    }
    drawCharts();
  }

  function restartStats() {
    brightness.fill(0);
    averaged = 0;
    statsStart = stepCount;
  }

  // Empty the tank
  function clear() {
    epoch++;
    const zeros = new Float32Array(cells);
    for (const buffer of heights) device.queue.writeBuffer(buffer, 0, zeros);
    pebbles.length = 0;
    peakHistory.length = 0;
    peak = 0;
    restartStats();
  }

  function restartSource() {
    sourceStart = stepCount;
    restartStats();
  }

  function changeBarrier() {
    device.queue.writeBuffer(depthBuffer, 0, buildDepth(barrierInput.value));
    clear();
    // Something to see, to the left of any barrier
    if (sourceInput.value === "pebbles") drop(100, H / 2);
  }

  function changeSource() {
    restartSource();
    if (sourceInput.value === "pebbles") drop(100, H / 2);
  }

  const on = (element, handler) => {
    element.addEventListener("input", handler);
    invalidation.then(() => element.removeEventListener("input", handler));
  };
  on(barrierInput, changeBarrier);
  on(sourceInput, changeSource);
  on(wavelengthInput, restartSource);
  // Once the numbers have blown up there is nothing left to save: start again
  on(courantInput, () => (peak > 1e3 ? clear() : restartStats()));

  changeBarrier();
  drop(W / 2, H / 2);

  const clearButton = ui.button({ label: "Clear", onClick: clear });
  const readout = ui.readout();
  drawCharts();

  let owed = 0; // steps due but not yet done
  let lastTime = null;
  const groups = { x: Math.ceil(W / groupSide), y: Math.ceil(H / groupSide) };

  function frame(ms) {
    const dt = lastTime === null ? 0 : Math.min((ms - lastTime) / 1000, 0.1);
    lastTime = ms;
    const C = courantInput.value;
    const lambda = wavelengthInput.value;
    const planeOn = sourceInput.value === "plane";

    // Waves travel at the chosen speed whatever the Courant number: a smaller one
    // just means more, smaller steps
    owed += ((10 ** speedInput.value) / C) * dt;
    const count = Math.min(Math.floor(owed), 40);
    owed = Math.min(owed - count, 1);

    const splashes = pebbles.splice(0, maxSplashes);

    paramU32[0] = W;
    paramU32[1] = H;
    paramF32[2] = C * C;
    paramF32[3] = 0.3 * C; // damping per step at the edge: a wave crosses the beach once
    paramF32[4] = beachWidth;
    paramU32[6] = planeOn ? 1 : 0;
    paramU32[7] = sourceX;
    paramF32[8] = (4 * Math.PI * C * C * amplitude) / lambda;
    paramF32[9] = (2 * Math.PI * C) / lambda;
    paramU32[10] = sourceStart;
    paramF32[11] = (3 * lambda) / C;
    paramU32[12] = splashes.length;
    paramF32[13] = 2.5;
    splashes.forEach((s, n) => paramF32.set(s, 16 + 4 * n));
    device.queue.writeBuffer(paramBuffer, 0, paramBytes);

    const encoder = device.createCommandEncoder();
    const compute = encoder.beginComputePass();
    if (splashes.length) {
      compute.setPipeline(splashPipeline);
      compute.setBindGroup(0, splashGroups[turn]);
      compute.dispatchWorkgroups(groups.x, groups.y);
    }
    for (let s = 0; s < count; s++) {
      compute.setPipeline(stepPipeline);
      compute.setBindGroup(0, stepGroups[turn]);
      compute.dispatchWorkgroups(groups.x, groups.y);
      compute.setPipeline(tickPipeline);
      compute.setBindGroup(0, tickGroup);
      compute.dispatchWorkgroups(1);
      turn = (turn + 1) % 3;
    }
    compute.end();
    stepCount += count;

    const sample = !readback.pending && ++frameCount % sampleEvery === 0;
    if (sample) {
      encoder.copyBufferToBuffer(heights[(turn + 1) % 3], 0, snapshot, 0, cells * 4);
      readback.copy(encoder);
    }

    const pass = gpu.beginRenderPass(encoder, context);
    pass.setPipeline(showPipeline);
    pass.setBindGroup(0, showGroups[turn]);
    pass.setVertexBuffer(0, cornerBuffer);
    pass.draw(6);
    pass.end();
    device.queue.submit([encoder.finish()]);

    if (sample) {
      const mine = epoch;
      readback.read((buffer) => {
        if (mine === epoch) onData(buffer);
      });
    }

    if (frameCount % 6 === 0) {
      const state = peak > 1e3 ? " · unstable" : "";
      readout.textContent = `${stepCount.toLocaleString()} steps · largest wave ${peak.toFixed(2)}${state}`;
    }
  }

  gpu.run(invalidation, device, frame);

  // The canvas with the controls laid over its corner
  yield ui.stage(canvas, [
    sourceInput,
    barrierInput,
    wavelengthInput,
    speedInput,
    courantInput,
    clearButton,
    readout,
  ]);
}
```


## A very old picture

Christiaan Huygens said, in a treatise published in 1690, that
every point on a wave can be treated as a new source of little circular waves, and that
the wave a moment later is what they add up to. A gap in a wall is then easy to understand:
the wave arrives, the points in the gap each start a ring, and nothing is left to cancel
the rings except one another. Two gaps are two sets of rings.

Around 1800 to 1803 Thomas Young used the same picture to argue that light is a wave.
In his lectures he showed what two sets of water waves do in a shallow tank, with a
lamp underneath, and then showed that light passed through two slits makes bright and
dark bands of the same kind. That is the double slit in the tank above, and it is still
the standard way to show waves in a classroom.

## How the computer makes ripples

The tank is a grid of 640 by 360 cells, and each cell holds one number: the height of the
water there. The rule is the same one a ball on a spring follows. A cell is pulled
towards the average of its four neighbours, and it carries on moving the way it was
already going. That is all a wave is, in the end: each cell is pulled by its neighbours,
and they are pulled by it.

To step forward in time the rule needs three things for every cell: its height now, its
height one step ago, and the heights of its four neighbours now. The GPU takes one thread
per cell, all 230,400 of them at once, and writes each cell's new height into a third
array. Then the three arrays swap roles, with no copying: "the one before" becomes
"the one before that", "now" becomes "the one before", and the new heights become
"now".

The walls and the open water are the same rule. Each cell has a number, 1 for water and
0 for wall, and the rule uses it when a cell looks at its neighbours. A wall is a cell
with nothing to pull on. There is no special case for a barrier, which is why a gap or a
slit costs nothing extra.

At the edges the tank has beaches. Close to the border, the rule gets a little damping
that grows towards the edge, so a wave that reaches it slowly dies instead of bouncing
back. Without them the surface soon becomes a mess. Real ripple tanks often have
sloping edges or sponge for the same reason.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## The wave equation, and the update

With the height written $u(x, y, t)$ and the wave speed $c$, the wave equation is

$$\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial t^2} = c^2 \, \nabla^2 u.$$

On a grid with spacing $\Delta x$ and time step $\Delta t$, each cell is updated with

$$u^{n+1}_{ij} = 2 u^n_{ij} - u^{n-1}_{ij} + C^2 \sum_{\text{4 neighbours}} k \left( u^n_{\text{nb}} - u^n_{ij} \right),$$

where $C = c \, \Delta t / \Delta x$ is the Courant number, and $k$ is 1 for a link
between two water cells and 0 for a link that touches a wall. A link with $k = 0$ pulls on
nothing, which is what makes a wall reflect.
:::

## Why the timestep has a limit

Try the **Courant number** slider. It is the distance a ripple travels in one step,
measured in cells. The waves on the screen move at the same speed whatever it says,
because **Wave speed** is in cells a second, so the slider only changes how finely
time is cut up. Make it small and nothing changes but the cost. Make it larger than 0.707
and the tank blows up: a fine red and blue checkerboard starts where the waves are made,
spreads across the tank and grows without limit.

This was found before there were computers. In 1928 Richard Courant, Kurt Friedrichs and
Hans Lewy, at Göttingen, were not trying to simulate anything. They wanted to prove that
the equations of mathematical physics have solutions at all, by replacing them with
grids and showing the grids converge. In doing so they noticed a limit. A cell only hears
from its neighbours each step, so the numbers on the grid can only know about a
ripple that has had time to reach them. If a real ripple can get further in one step than
the grid can listen, the grid is deaf to something that matters, and the answer cannot
be right.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Trefethen's 13, no. 2

This is the second paper on [Nick Trefethen's list of 13 classic papers in applied
mathematics](https://web.stanford.edu/class/cme324/classics/): Courant, Friedrichs and
Lewy, 1928.
:::

The picture is this. In one step a cell hears from the four cells next to it, so it
can listen to a diamond, one cell out along the axes. A ripple travels a circle of
radius $C$ cells in that step. The circle must fit inside the diamond.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  // The stencil diamond and the circle a ripple covers in one step
  const unit = 70;
  const size = 2 * unit * 1.25;
  const limit = 1 / Math.SQRT2;
  const bad = courant > limit;
  const mid = size / 2;
  return html`<svg viewBox="0 0 ${size} ${size}" width="${size}" height="${size}"
      style="max-width: 100%; display: block; margin: 0 auto;" role="img"
      aria-label="The four-neighbour stencil as a diamond, with a circle of radius equal to the Courant number">
    <polygon points="${mid},${mid - unit} ${mid + unit},${mid} ${mid},${mid + unit} ${mid - unit},${mid}"
      fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-opacity="0.7" stroke-width="2"/>
    <circle cx="${mid}" cy="${mid}" r="${unit * limit}" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"
      stroke-opacity="0.3" stroke-dasharray="4 3"/>
    <circle cx="${mid}" cy="${mid}" r="${unit * courant}" fill="${bad ? "#FF4834" : "#3a9ad9"}"
      fill-opacity="0.35" stroke="${bad ? "#FF4834" : "#3a9ad9"}" stroke-width="2"/>
    <text x="${mid}" y="${size - 6}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="currentColor"
      font-family="system-ui, sans-serif">C = ${courant.toFixed(2)}${bad ? ": too big" : ""}</text>
  </svg>`;
}
```

The diamond is what the grid can hear. The coloured circle is how far a ripple gets in
a step. The dashed circle just touches the diamond's sides, at $C = 1/\sqrt{2} \approx 0.707$,
and past that the circle pokes out of the diamond and the grid is deaf. The same
number turns out to be the exact point at which the rule becomes unstable, which is
not obvious in advance, and which a short calculation confirms.

## Analysis

_Left._ The brightness of the waves along the far wall of the tank, with a plane
wave through the **Gap** or the **Double slit**. The solid line is what the tank gives,
averaged over many moments, and the dashed line is the classic prediction for
two slits of width $a$ a distance $d$ apart, a long way from the screen. It has two
parts. The fine fringes come from the two slits, bright where the paths from them
differ by a whole number of wavelengths, $d \sin\theta = m\lambda$. The broad hump
they sit under comes from the width of each slit. Change the **Wavelength** and both
move, in the way the formula says. The two do not agree exactly, because the far wall
is not very far away and the tank is two-dimensional.

_Right._ The largest wave height in the tank as time goes by, on a logarithmic scale. A
pebble's wave fades, a plane wave holds steady, and above $C = 0.707$ the line goes
straight up, because the error is multiplied by the same number at every step. A
straight line on a log scale is exponential growth.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| column: page
charts = {
  // Two empty hosts; the simulation cell above draws into them as data arrives
  const ui = await import(new URL("../lib/ui.js", document.baseURI).href);
  return ui.chartHosts(["screen", "peak"]);
}
```

## What the tank leaves out

Every wavelength in this tank travels at the same speed, so a ring keeps its shape as
it spreads. Real water is not so well behaved. Long waves on deep water travel faster
than short ones, and the little ripples of a real tank are partly driven by surface
tension, so the tank above is the idealised case, closest to long waves in shallow
water. The next step is to let the speed depend on the wavelength, and to see what that
does to the pattern behind a ship.
